captions.caption: A man shows wood shavings and logs prepared for a fire at night.
The flashlight scans across organized piles of firewood of varying sizes.
The camera pans over the different thicknesses of wood sticks on a log.
A close-up view of wood shavings in a camouflage-patterned container.
The man explains his preparation of shavings and pencil-sized sticks.
The flashlight illuminates a row of sticks ranging from thin to thick.
The man points out the "pencil" sized sticks among the firewood.
The light moves across the wood as the man says "bigger, bigger, bigger".
The camera focuses on the largest split wood pieces at the end of the line.
The man identifies the front log used for the long fire setup.
The flashlight scans the length of the front log on the ground.
The camera pans across the space between two parallel long logs.
The man points out the rear log used in his fire arrangement.
The light follows the parallel logs into the darkness.
A small green container is visible resting on one of the logs.
The camera returns to the main area of wood preparation.
The flashlight highlights the ground where the fire will be built.
The man mentions that this setup is for a specific type of fire.
The camera shows the neatly arranged firewood on the base log.
The man states he will not be lighting the fire just yet.
The light remains on the camouflage container filled with wood shavings.
The camera stays focused on the prepared firewood and logs.
The video cuts to the man preparing to strike a fire starter.
The man is kneeling in the dark with a headlamp on.
He holds a ferrocerium rod and a striker over the pile of shavings.
The man positions his hands to strike sparks into the kindling.
He strikes the ferro rod, sending a few initial sparks flying.
Another strike produces more sparks that land on the wood shavings.
He continues to strike the rod vigorously against the striker.
A bright shower of sparks is directed into the center of the shavings.
The man pauses for a moment to check if the shavings have caught.
He leans in closer to the firewood setup with his headlamp.
He places the tip of the ferro rod directly into the shavings.
A forceful strike creates a large flash and ignites the shavings.
A small, steady flame begins to grow from the wood shavings.
The man watches as the fire takes hold in the prepared kindling.
The orange glow of the fire starts to illuminate the surrounding logs.
The man uses a small stick to adjust the burning shavings.
He carefully adds more fine shavings to the small flame.
The fire grows larger and begins to produce more light.
He uses his hands to shelter the young flame from the wind.
The man continues to nurture the fire by adding more fuel.
He carefully places more wood shavings onto the growing fire.
The flames spread through the pile of shavings on the log.
The man adjusts the position of the burning material for better airflow.
The fire is now burning consistently in the center of the logs.
He gently blows on the base of the fire to increase its intensity.
The flames rise higher as more of the kindling catches fire.
The man continues to tend to the fire with his hands.
The fire is well-established and glowing brightly in the dark.
He starts to reach for the small sticks he had prepared earlier.
He carefully places thin sticks over the burning shavings.
The small sticks begin to ignite, adding more volume to the fire.
The man mentions that it is about 7:20 PM and very dark out.
He adds a bundle of very thin twigs to the established flames.
Thick white smoke rises as the new twigs begin to burn.
The fire flares up significantly as the thin twigs catch fire.
He adds more small sticks to further build up the fire.
The man says he will likely stay up until 10 or 11 PM.
The fire is now burning brightly, casting light on the nearby logs.
